chunks: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibrahim Al-Hazza', from Muhammad Bin Sagheer, from his grandfather Shuayb who said,
'I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The world is a prison for the Momin, so which prison is it that any good came from it?''

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life; the transient, lower realm of existence as opposed to the eternal hereafter
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer (mu'min); one who possesses true iman (faith) and lives in accordance with it
key_terms.جَاءَ: came; issued or proceeded from, used in the rhetorical question to underscore the absence of real good originating from a prison
key_terms.خَيْرٌ: good; genuine benefit or goodness, rhetorically negated here to emphasise the inherently adverse nature of worldly life
key_terms.سِجْنُ: prison; a place of confinement and restriction, used here as a metaphor for the trials and limitations imposed upon the believer in this world

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) say about the nature of the worldly life for a believer (mu'min)?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) declares that the worldly life (al-dunya) is a prison for the believer (mu'min), confining him with trials, afflictions, and restrictions. The rhetorical question — 'which prison is it that any good came from it?' — emphatically negates the notion that the world can be a source of true benefit for the faithful, directing their aspirations toward the eternal abode of the hereafter. This narration contextualises within the broader Shia ethical tradition of detachment from worldly life (zuhd) and patient endurance of its hardships.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibrahim Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Sagheer, from his grandfather Shuayb who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The world is a prison for the Momin, so which prison is it that any good came from it?’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ibrahim al-Hadhdha’ from Muhammad ibn Saghir from his grandfather, Shu’ayb who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘This world is a prison for believing people. Which prison is it wherein anything good may exist?”
